Package neqsim.standards.oilquality

Class Standard_ASTM_D6377

java.lang.Object
neqsim.util.NamedBaseClass
neqsim.standards.Standard
neqsim.standards.oilquality.Standard_ASTM_D6377
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, StandardInterface, NamedInterface
public class Standard_ASTM_D6377 extends Standard
EOS screening of VPCR4, correlated RVP-equivalent values and bubble-point TVP.

The default is raw VPCR4: vapor/liquid volume ratio 4:1, not 80% molar vapor. The D6377-labelled correlation is 0.834 * VPCR4; D323-82 is 0.752 * VPCR4 + 0.0607 in bara. VPCR4_no_water and the historical D323-73/79 label both return raw dry VPCR4. These model labels do not certify laboratory equivalence or compliance; isOnSpec() always returns true.

calculate() mutates the supplied fluid state. A clone protects temperature, pressure and composition during this workflow, but BIP arrays can be shared across clones: do not mutate model parameters through a clone. The water-free variants remove water only when it is the last component and otherwise keep it as a 1e-15 trace, because component removal does not remap BIPs when retained component indices shift. A finite positive Standard_ASTM_D6377.RvpResult alone does not certify convergence to the corrected volume-ratio target, except for Standard_ASTM_D6377.RvpMethod.RVP_ASTM_D6377_ADD_WATER_SATURATED, which checks it.

For a declared water-contact storage basis, Standard_ASTM_D6377.RvpMethod.RVP_ASTM_D6377_ADD_WATER_SATURATED returns RVPE_water_sat = 0.834 * (VPCR4_dry + psat_water(37.8 C)), always at 37.8 C, not dry RVPE plus the full water pressure. The EOS only sees the water-free hydrocarbon liquid; the water term is the IAPWS-IF97 Region 4 pure-water saturation pressure and is always added, whether or not the fluid contains water. This assumes water activity near one and sufficient water for saturation; it neither models the ASTM apparatus nor repairs sampling losses. The analogous TVP approximation is TVP_dry(T) + psat_water(T). See the vapor-pressure water-basis guide.

      public Standard_ASTM_D6377.RvpResult getRvpResult()
      Returns a structured RVP result for the currently configured method.

      Returns:

    • getRvpResult

      public Standard_ASTM_D6377.RvpResult getRvpResult(Standard_ASTM_D6377.RvpMethod method)
      Returns a structured RVP result for a specific method.

      Call calculate() first. Direct correlations reuse that calculation; water-free variants run extra flashes lazily on first access. Dry-basis selection is separate from correlation selection: multiply raw dry VPCR4 by 0.834 explicitly for dry D6377-labelled RVPE. Only Standard_ASTM_D6377.RvpMethod.RVP_ASTM_D6377_ADD_WATER_SATURATED adds an independent water-saturation term; it is always evaluated at 37.8 C and reports that temperature.

      Parameters:
      method - the method whose result should be returned; must not be null
      Returns:
      the structured RVP result for the requested method
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if method is null

    • calculateNoWaterVariants

      private void calculateNoWaterVariants()
      Evaluates the water-free vapor-pressure variants VPCR4_no_water and RVP_ASTM_D323_73_79.

      This requires a water-free clone of the fluid (see createWaterFreeFluid(SystemInterface)) plus a bubble-point flash and an 80% vapor-volume flash, which roughly doubles the cost of calculate(). Because most callers only read VPCR4 or RVP_ASTM_D6377, the work is deferred until one of the water-free values is actually requested and is then cached until the next calculate() call.

    • calculateAddWaterSaturated

      private void calculateAddWaterSaturated()
      Evaluates Standard_ASTM_D6377.RvpMethod.RVP_ASTM_D6377_ADD_WATER_SATURATED at the fixed RVP reference temperature.

      RVPE = 0.834 * (VPCR4_dry(37.8 C) + psat_water,IF97(37.8 C)) in bara. The EOS only evaluates the water-free hydrocarbon fluid; the water contribution is the IAPWS-IF97 pure-water saturation pressure, added whether or not the fluid contains water (assumed water-saturated storage). The result is NaN when the dry flash fails, does not end with exactly one gas and one oil phase, or misses the corrected gas volume fraction of 0.8 (V/L = 4) by more than 1.0E-4. The user-set reference temperature is ignored: RVP is defined at 37.8 C.

    • createWaterFreeFluid

      private static SystemInterface createWaterFreeFluid(SystemInterface source)
      Returns a water-free working copy of a fluid for the dry VPCR4 flash.

      Removing a component compacts the component list without remapping the EOS binary interaction parameter (BIP) matrix. Removing water is therefore only safe when it is the last component, because no retained index shifts. When water sits elsewhere, removal would silently give hydrocarbon pairs the wrong BIPs, so water is kept as a trace of mole fraction 1.0E-15 instead. At that level the water contribution to the flash is negligible (VPCR4 agrees with the truly water-free fluid to about 13 significant digits) and every BIP stays on its original pair. The working copy is reset to its unflashed state before water is touched. The source fluid is not modified.

      Parameters:
      source - fluid that may contain water
      Returns:
      a clone with water removed (water last) or reduced to a trace (water not last)
